one_line_contribution: A budget-matched re-examination of agentic memory: it asks whether the documented harm of injected retrieved experience, and the reported gains of curation methods (A-MEM-style organization, MemHarness-style reconstruction), are artifacts of injected token volume rather than content, using length-matched decoy arms (C2/C2u/C3/C4/C5) and per-instance token-matched raw-retrieval baselines (C8a/C8b) plus a compression-only rewrite (C9). The new thing is a control and the table it produces, not a method — which is a legitimate contribution but a thin one.
closest_prior_work: Two, and the proposal engages only one. (a) Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297) — the proposal names it and the rebuttal is fair: procedural, non-answer-bearing injected content removes the signal-loss term, so the prediction genuinely differs. (b) The in-context-learning demonstration-ablation line — Min et al., 'Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations' (random/incorrect labels retain most of the gain), and the several follow-ups showing ICL gains saturate at small k — is not cited anywhere in Related Work or the collision check. This is the more dangerous omission, because the injected memory items occupy exactly the demonstration slot, and 'content contributes far less than you think; returns saturate after a couple of exemplars' is precisely that literature's headline. A reviewer will read 'content value saturates after one item' as a decade-old ICL result transplanted to agent memory. It does not fully scoop the proposal — retriever-selected, topically-correct, procedural trajectories in a ReAct loop are not labeled classification demonstrations, and the curation re-examination table is genuinely absent from that line — but the proposal must argue this explicitly rather than not mention it, and its novelty score suffers accordingly.
strongest_objection: Predictions 1, 2 and 3 are all ratios or offsets defined against a harm effect the design never establishes will exist above its own noise floor. Prediction 1 is '(C2(7) recovers >=60% of the accuracy drop of C1(7) relative to C1(1))'; prediction 2 bounds the relevant-vs-decoy offset at <3 points, i.e. below the stated E1 MDE of ~4 points; prediction 3 is a null. The motivating pilot (7->3 items removes harm) came from a different scaffold with single-digit break counts, and E1 as specified — HotpotQA/MuSiQue multi-hop with ~3k prompt tokens and seven short items — is not a regime where token load plausibly bites. If C1(7) minus C1(1) on E1 is 2-3 points rather than 8, then every headline prediction is a ratio of two sub-MDE quantities and the paper has no result in either direction; the grid contains no contingency arm and the pre-registration says nothing about what happens in that case. Compounding this: analysis (c) promises 'approximately parallel curves' for the relevant and decoy arms, but the grid instantiates the relevant arm at three token levels (C1(1), C1(3), C1(7)) and the decoy arm at exactly one (C2(7); C2u(7) is a different bank, not a second budget point). Parallelism cannot be assessed from a one-point curve, and the paper's title claim — that content value is exhausted at one item — has no matched one-item decoy control (no C2(1)) to measure the k=1 offset against. The central figure and the title rest on arms that are not in the grid.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add C2(1) and C2(3) so the decoy arm is a curve rather than a point, and state a pre-registered decision rule for the case where the C1(7)-vs-C1(1) harm on E1 fails to clear the MDE — including a power analysis for the ratio in prediction 1, not just for a single delta (a 60%-recovery ratio at n=600 needs a base effect near 8-10 points to be estimable). (2) Add the upward token match (see missing_baseline). (3) Pre-register a TOST margin for the coefficient-equality claim in analysis (b) as you already did for prediction 4; 'significantly negative and statistically indistinguishable from each other' is currently a null tested by failure to reject, which is the exact failure the research track's own brief calls out. Note also that with only ~6 distinct design points the three regressors (relevant tokens, decoy tokens, item count) are near-collinear and the mixed-effects fit is close to a reparameterization of the condition means — say what it buys over the paired McNemar contrasts. (4) Specify the C8a/C8b matching rule: 'selected/truncated to match' is ambiguous, and mid-trajectory truncation of raw experience damages the baseline in a way unrelated to token count, so a curation win under C8 would be uninterpretable. Prefer selection-only matching with truncation as a reported fallback. (5) Analyze the fidelity gate's own noise: a 100-instance dev split has an MDE well above 10 points, so 'reproduces a positive delta in rough magnitude' is close to a coin flip and silently selects which methods enter the headline table. (6) Correct the claim that the position ablation is 'free — reuses the same episodes with one extra rendering'. Moving memory from the prompt head to before the action step changes every subsequent rollout; it requires re-running the 8 decisive conditions, roughly 4,800 additional episodes, about a third of E1 primary.
missing_baseline: The symmetric, upward token match: pad the curated output of C7a/C7b back up to C1(7)'s token count with neutral filler and re-run. The plan only ever matches downward (shrink raw to the curated budget), which confounds 'raw at low budget' with 'raw damaged by truncation/selection'. The load hypothesis makes a sharp, cheap prediction here — inflating the curated output to raw length should destroy most of the curation gain — and its failure would refute the account far more directly than C8 can confirm it. Two smaller omissions a reviewer will also demand: C0 padded to C7a's length (no-memory-but-same-tokens, which separates 'tokens' from 'memory tokens' at the curation comparison), and a random-single-item-from-bank control at k=1, without which BudgetFirst's 'tuned k=1 raw retrieval is competitive' cannot be distinguished from the stronger and quite different claim that any single item is competitive.
preprint_collision: Above average in candor: it names a concrete methodological threat (Distractor-Aware Truncation, arXiv:2608.03297), states honestly that it would be scooped if that group extended to agent memory, and discloses that coverage is six queries because the search tool hit its call limit. That disclosure is the right behavior and I credit it. It is nevertheless not sufficient for a proposal whose entire contribution is the assertion 'nobody ran this control'. Three problems. First, the one search that decides whether the contribution exists — whether A-MEM's or MemHarness's own appendices already contain a length- or token-matched raw baseline — is explicitly not performed; the proposal instead pre-concedes that such an appendix ablation 'would reduce our contribution' and moves on. That specific check is cheap and mandatory. Second, the claim 'none of the retrieved papers reports a comparison in which the uncurated baseline is matched on injected tokens' is asserted for five papers without per-paper evidence, and it is doing all the novelty work. Third, the check searched agent-memory and long-context RAG but not the ICL demonstration-ablation literature, which is where the 'content matters less than volume; gains saturate at small k' claim already lives; that is a search-scope failure, not a framing choice. No preprint I can name already makes the specific claim about agent-memory curation methods, so I do not judge this scooped — but the novelty case is under-evidenced rather than established, and I score it as a weakness.
